title: DOW-UAP-D083, Narrative Statement 5, Western United States Event, 2023
what_is_it: First-hand witness narrative memorandum submitted to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) documenting UAP observations by a federal law enforcement special agent.
core_summary: Witness 5, a U.S. federal law enforcement special agent, reported observing multiple UAP events over two days in October 2023 in the western United States. On the first evening, the witness observed a large orange light hovering over a ridge, followed by a large red orb that released smaller red orbs, accompanied by white flashes. The following morning, the witness encountered a red-and-white light pair near ground level that moved laterally at 15-20 mph with zero resistance, and later observed a formation of faint lights that appeared to evade detection, along with unexplained symmetrical ground markings near the sighting location.
interpretation_warnings: Heavy redaction throughout: specific dates, names, locations, coordinates, license plates, and institutional identifiers are systematically redacted, preventing independent verification of the location and participants.
Single-source narrative: this is one witness's account among several agents present, and no corroborating witness statements are included in this document.
Observations occurred in low-light and nighttime conditions, which can affect visual perception and identification of objects.
The witness acknowledges uncertainty in several places (e.g., 'I think', 'may have', 'I could not judge how far away'), indicating honest but imprecise recollection.
No sensor data, photographs, or video are included despite a camera being deployed; only hand-drawn sketches accompany the narrative.
The radio anomaly (one-way communication) is reported secondhand based on post-event debriefing, not confirmed by technical analysis.
The ground markings were observed hours after the sighting and their connection to the UAP events is implied but not established.

public_headline: Federal Agent Reports Multiple Unexplained Lights Over Western US in 2023
public_tldr: This Department of War document is a first-hand witness statement submitted to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) by a federal law enforcement agent who observed multiple unexplained aerial phenomena over two days in October 2023 in the western United States. The witness describes hovering lights, a red orb that released smaller orbs, a low-altitude light pair that moved laterally without resistance, and unexplained ground markings — but the document is heavily redacted and includes no sensor data or corroborating witness accounts.
public_narrative:
This document, dated 2 June 2026 and signed by AARO Director Jon T. Kosloski, contains the narrative statement of "Witness 5," one of several U.S. federal law enforcement special agents who reported observing unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) over two days in October 2023 in the western United States. It was submitted to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, the Pentagon body responsible for investigating UAP reports.

On the first evening, the witness reported seeing a large orange light hovering over a ridge at 6:58 PM with zero resistance or movement, lasting about a minute. Twenty minutes later, at 7:18 PM, a large red orb appeared and released two smaller red orbs that moved westward; all lights vanished within roughly ten seconds. The red orb reappeared at 7:37 PM, and a white flash of light was observed in the western sky. The witness also reported a radio anomaly during this period: other teams could not hear transmissions from the witness's group.

The following morning, around 4:30 AM, the witness observed a pair of lights — one white and square, one round and red — hovering two to three feet above the ground. The light pair moved laterally at an estimated 15–20 mph with zero resistance or change in height. After the lights switched off, night vision goggles revealed a thin horizontal line roughly four feet wide. Later, the witness observed a formation of faint lights moving together in a precise pattern that appeared to shift position as if trying to blend into the stars. Near the sighting location, symmetrical round scrapes were found in the dirt, described as fresh and sharp despite calm conditions the previous night.

The document is heavily redacted throughout: specific dates, names, locations, coordinates, and institutional identifiers have been removed, making independent verification impossible. No photographs, video, or sensor data accompany the narrative — only hand-drawn sketches. The statement is a single witness's account; no corroborating statements from the other agents present are included in this document. The witness openly acknowledges uncertainty in several observations. AARO has not published any analytical conclusion about these events within this document.
public_caveats: This is a single witness's account. Other agents were present but their statements are not included in this document, so there is no corroboration within it.
